meta.description: Chat, image and video generation API, compatible with OpenAI. One API key for muse-chat, muse-image and muse-video. Pay as you go.
meta.og_title: Muse API — chat, image and video generation
meta.og_description: OpenAI-compatible: just change base_url and your API key.

hero.title: Chat, image and video AI
hero.lede: Three models ready for your product — muse-chat, muse-image and muse-video. OpenAI-compatible: keep the SDK you already use and just change base_url.

features.compat_text: Same request and response format as OpenAI. Works with the OpenAI SDKs, LobeChat, Cherry Studio, ChatGPT-Next-Web and more.
features.stream_text: Chat replies arrive chunk by chunk over Server-Sent Events, so you can show the answer while it is being written.
features.async_text: Images and videos run in the background: create a task, get an ID, poll for progress. No proxy or client timeouts.
features.refs_text: Send up to 4 images to keep a character, product or layout. Transparent PNG output when you need it.

models.title: Three models for chat, images and video
models.lede: Pick a model with the model parameter, just like with OpenAI. One API key works for all of them.
models.chat_text: A multi-turn assistant that also understands images in your messages.
models.image_text: Generate images from a text prompt, or from reference images you attach.
models.image_2: Up to 4 reference images per request
models.image_3: Transparent PNG when you need it
models.image_4: Returned as a URL or base64
models.video_text: Generate video from a text prompt, or from an image used as the first frame.
models.video_3: Runs as a task with progress tracking
models.alias_note: To plug into existing tools quickly, familiar model names such as gpt-4o, dall-e-3 or sora are also accepted and routed to the matching Muse model. See the full list in the docs.

pricing.title: Simple, pay-as-you-go pricing
pricing.lede: Top up credit once and use it across every model. Each successful request is deducted from your balance — failed requests are never charged.
pricing.image_2: Transparent background at no extra cost
pricing.video_2: Billed on the duration you request
pricing.chat_2: Token usage and cost in every response
pricing.note: Prices in USD. Check your balance at any time with GET /v1/balance; every response includes its cost_usd.

how.title: Up and running in minutes
how.s1_text: Open Buy credit, pick how much credit you want (from ${{topup.min}}) and enter your email.
how.s2_text: Pay with PayPal or a debit or credit card. Your API key (m2a-…) appears instantly with the credit loaded. It is shown only once, so store it safely.
how.s3_text: Set base_url to {{base_code}} and make your first request. The docs have complete examples.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q_code: Do I need to change my code?
faq.a_code: No. If you already use an OpenAI SDK or an app that supports an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set the base URL to {{base_code}} and swap in your API key. Requests and responses keep the same format.
faq.a_billing: Images cost {{price.image}} each, video {{price.video_second}} per requested second, and chat {{price.chat_input}} per 1M input tokens and {{price.chat_output}} per 1M output tokens. You are charged only when a request succeeds: if a generation fails, the reserved amount is refunded automatically.
faq.q_balance: How do I check my balance, and what happens when it runs out?
faq.a_balance: Call GET /v1/balance with your key at any time. When the balance is too low for a request, the API answers HTTP 402 with insufficient_balance until you top up — nothing is charged.
faq.q_time: How long does an image or video take?
faq.a_time: An image usually takes 1–2 minutes and a video longer; it can be slower at peak times. That is why we recommend async tasks ("async": true for images, always on for video) and polling for the result instead of holding one connection open.
faq.q_storage: How long are generated files kept?
faq.a_storage: Results are returned as random, hard-to-guess URLs. Download and store them on your side right away — links are not guaranteed to last. For images you can also get base64 directly with "response_format": "b64_json".
faq.q_apps: Which chat apps work with it?
faq.a_apps: Any app that lets you configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: LobeChat, Cherry Studio, ChatGPT-Next-Web, Open WebUI… Enter the base URL and your API key. See Integrations in the docs.
faq.q_keys: Can my team use several keys?
faq.a_keys: Yes. Ask us for one key per app or teammate; each key has its own balance and can be revoked on its own.

meta.description: Muse API docs: authentication, chat completions, image and video generation, async tasks, billing and errors. OpenAI-compatible.

hero.lede: Muse API provides chat, image generation and video generation through OpenAI-compatible endpoints. If you already use an OpenAI SDK, just change base_url and your API key — requests and responses keep the same format.

quickstart.step1: Buy credit with PayPal or a card and get an API key (m2a-…) instantly.
quickstart.step2: Install the OpenAI SDK: pip install openai or npm install openai.
quickstart.step3: Point the client at Muse API and send your first request:

auth.intro: Every /v1/* endpoint (except result files) requires an API key, sent in either header:
auth.invalid: A missing, invalid or revoked key returns 401 with "code": "invalid_api_key".
auth.warning: Keep your key on the server. Never embed it in frontend code, mobile apps or public repositories — anyone holding the key can spend your balance. If a key leaks, email {{support_email}} to revoke it and get a new one.

models.intro: Choose a model with the model parameter. Each endpoint accepts only models of its own kind; leave model empty to use the endpoint's default.
models.chat_caps: Multi-turn chat, system prompts, streaming, image input
models.image_caps: Text-to-image, reference images (up to 4), transparent background
models.aliases_intro: So that existing tools work without reconfiguration, the names below are accepted and routed to the matching Muse model. They are aliases only — the request is still served by the Muse model.
models.fallback: Model names not on the list fall back to the endpoint's default model. Sending a model of the wrong kind (for example muse-video to chat) returns 400.

billing.intro: Muse API is prepaid: you top up USD credit to your API key and each successful request is deducted from that balance.
billing.image_basis: Each generated image; n images cost n × the price. Transparent background costs nothing extra.
billing.video_basis: The duration you request (duration / seconds), or 10 seconds if you don't set one — a 10-second video costs {{price.video_10s}}.
billing.chat_basis: Prompt tokens (the messages you send) and completion tokens (the reply).
billing.how_media: Images and video: the price is reserved when the request is accepted. If generation fails, is cancelled or is interrupted, the full amount is refunded automatically.
billing.how_chat: Chat: charged when the reply finishes, for the tokens actually used. A streamed reply that you stop early is charged for the output produced so far.
billing.how_free: Failed requests are free. Errors such as 400, 401, 402 or a failed generation never cost anything.
billing.how_cost: Every response shows its cost: usage.cost_usd for chat, cost_usd for images and on every task object.
billing.tokens_note: Tokens are counted by the gateway: about 4 characters per token for Latin-script text and 1 token per Chinese, Japanese or Korean character. The same numbers are returned in usage, so what you see is what you pay.
billing.topup: To top up, open /billing and pay with PayPal or a debit or credit card — the credit is added instantly, to a new key or to one you already have. For invoices or other payment methods, email {{support_email}}. Check your remaining credit at any time with GET /v1/balance. When the balance is too low for a request, the API answers 402 insufficient_balance and nothing is charged.

chat.intro: Compatible with OpenAI's client.chat.completions.create(), both streaming and non-streaming.
chat.p_messages: The conversation history. role is system (or developer), user or assistant. content is a string, or an array of {"type": "text"} and {"type": "image_url"} parts (see image input).
chat.p_stream: Return the reply in chunks over Server-Sent Events.
chat.p_stream_options: {"include_usage": true} adds a final chunk with usage (including cost_usd).
chat.p_user: A stable ID for one conversation (for example your chat session ID). Sending the same value on follow-up turns makes replies faster. Always send the full messages history anyway.
chat.p_ignored: Accepted for compatibility but currently have no effect.
chat.usage_note: usage holds the billed token counts and cost_usd, the amount deducted for this request.
chat.stream_intro: With "stream": true the response is text/event-stream: each data: line carries a chat.completion.chunk, ending with data: [DONE].
chat.stream_error: If an error happens after the stream has started, the server sends a data: {"error": {…}} event followed by data: [DONE]. Errors before the first content arrive as a normal HTTP status.
chat.vision_intro: Add an image_url part to content. The URL can be http(s)://… or a data URL data:image/png;base64,….

images.intro: Compatible with client.images.generate(). Generates images from a prompt, optionally with reference images.
images.p_prompt: Describes the image to create. With reference images, say how to use them (for example “keep the same character, move the scene to a beach”).
images.p_n: Number of images to create, 1 to 4. Each image is billed.
images.p_format: url returns a download link; b64_json returns the image base64-encoded inside the response.
images.p_background: transparent cuts out the subject and returns a transparent PNG (about 30 seconds extra per image, no extra charge). auto / opaque keep the image as generated.
images.p_image: One or up to 4 reference images: data URL, http(s) URL or a base64 string.
images.p_async: Return a task immediately and poll it, instead of waiting for the image. Recommended — see the note below.
images.async_warning: Use "async": true. An image usually takes 1–2 minutes and can take longer at peak times. A synchronous request keeps the connection open the whole time and may be cut by a proxy or HTTP client (commonly HTTP 524 after about 100 seconds). Async mode returns at once and has no such limit.
images.refs_intro: Send images in the image field to keep a character, product or style. For example, putting a product on a model:
images.async_intro: With "async": true the response is a task. Poll GET /v1/images/generations/{id} until status is succeeded; its result then has the same shape as the synchronous response above. In this mode images are always returned as url.

edits.intro: Compatible with client.images.edit(): upload image files as multipart/form-data instead of sending URLs. The images are used as references to create a new image.
edits.p_prompt: Describes the image to create from the references.
edits.p_mask: Not supported — a request with mask returns 400.

videos.intro: Video generation always runs as a task: POST returns a task right away, then poll GET /v1/videos/{id} until it finishes.
videos.p_duration: Desired length in seconds (1–60). This is what you are billed on ({{price.video_second}} per second); the actual clip length may differ slightly.
videos.p_image: An image to use as the first frame (image-to-video): data URL or http(s) URL.

tasks.intro: Video, and images in async mode, return a task. All tasks share this structure:
tasks.f_result: Present when succeeded. Images: {"created", "data": [{"url"}]}. Video: {"url", "mime", "width", "height"} (width / height may be null).
tasks.f_cost: The amount reserved for this task. It is refunded if the task ends failed or cancelled.
tasks.note: Polling every 5 seconds for images and every 10 seconds for video is plenty. Polling is free. Tasks are kept for a limited time, so save the result as soon as a task completes.

media.intro: Generated images and videos are returned as /v1/media/… URLs. This endpoint needs no API key, so the links can go straight into <img> / <video> tags; file names are random and cannot be guessed.
media.warning: Links are not guaranteed to last. Download the file and store it on your side as soon as you receive it.

balance.intro: Returns the remaining credit of the key making the request. unlimited is true for keys that are not billed, in which case balance_usd is null.

list_models.intro: Compatible with client.models.list(). Returns the models and compatible names; each entry also carries kind (chat / image / video), and compatible names carry alias_of.

errors.intro: Errors return an HTTP status with a body in the same format as OpenAI, so the SDKs raise the matching exception (AuthenticationError, BadRequestError, …):
errors.e400: Invalid parameters (missing prompt, more than 4 images, model of the wrong kind…)
errors.a400: Fix the request according to message; do not retry it unchanged
errors.e401: API key missing, invalid or revoked
errors.e402: Balance too low for this request (insufficient_balance); nothing was charged
errors.a404: Check the ID; old tasks may have been cleaned up
errors.a429: Retry after a few tens of seconds
errors.a502: Retry; if it keeps failing with the same prompt, rephrase the prompt
errors.a504: Retry; for images, switch to "async": true
errors.retry: For 429, 502, 503 and 504, retry with increasing backoff (for example 2 s, 5 s, 15 s). The server already retries internally before returning an error, so there is no need to retry aggressively. A failed task has status: "failed" and an error with the same meaning.

integrations.intro: Any app that supports an OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. Choose the OpenAI provider (or “OpenAI-compatible” / “Custom”) and enter:
integrations.lobechat: OpenAI provider → enter the API key and the API proxy URL (with /v1).
integrations.openwebui: Admin Settings → Connections → OpenAI API: URL with /v1.
integrations.cherry: Add an OpenAI-type provider; set API host to https://muse.isemi.io (the app adds /v1).
integrations.others: Use the OpenAI node / model and change the base URL.
integrations.manual_models: If an app does not fetch the model list by itself, add muse-chat manually (and muse-image if the app supports image generation).

limits.max_time_value: Chat 5 min · image 4 min · video 10 min (per attempt)
limits.first_token: Wait for the first chat token
limits.first_token_value: 45 seconds; after that the server retries automatically
limits.unknown_params: Unsupported parameters are ignored rather than rejected, so clients that send newer OpenAI fields keep working.
limits.unsupported: Not supported yet: /v1/responses (use /v1/chat/completions), tool / function calling, mask for image edits, embeddings and audio.
limits.policy: Content that violates the content policy may be refused; the request then returns an error instead of a result, and is not charged.

billing.title: Credit for every model, in a minute
billing.lede: Pay once with PayPal or a debit or credit card. Your credit is ready right away and works across chat, image and video — you get exactly the amount you pay.
billing.mode_new: New customer — get an API key
billing.email_hint: Names your key and lets support find your payment. No newsletters.
billing.key_hint: Starts with m2a-. Used only to find the key to credit.
billing.secure_note: Payments are processed securely by PayPal. Paying by card does not need a PayPal login. PayPal emails you a receipt.
billing.err_amount: Choose an amount from ${{topup.min}} to ${{topup.max}}, in whole cents.
billing.err_key: Paste your API key — it starts with m2a-.
billing.err_generic: The payment could not be completed. If PayPal charged you, email {{support_email}} with your receipt and we will sort it out.
billing.err_sdk: The payment buttons could not load. Disable any blocker for this page and reload, or email {{support_email}}.
billing.err_key_unknown: That API key was not found or has been revoked.
billing.err_declined: The payment was declined. Try another card or pay with PayPal.
billing.err_rate: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
billing.key_warning: Shown only once — store it now. We keep only a fingerprint of the key, so nobody can show it to you again.
billing.topup_done: The credit has been added to your key.
billing.pending: PayPal is still processing your payment. The credit is added automatically as soon as it clears.
billing.already: This payment was already credited. If you did not save your new key, email {{support_email}}.
billing.disabled_title: Online checkout is not available right now
billing.disabled_text: Email {{support_email}} with the amount of credit you want and we will set you up.
billing.sandbox_banner: SANDBOX — test mode. Payments here are simulated with PayPal sandbox test buyers. Do not use a real card.
billing.needs_support: Your payment went through, but the key it was for is no longer active, so the credit has not been applied yet. Email {{support_email}} with your PayPal receipt and we will sort it out.
